Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
Just a mecanic idea...

Name: Full Moon
Cardtype: Event
Moon. Transient.
Put this card in play with 3 counters. Werewolves have +1 bleed and +1 strength. Burn 1 counter from this card during your influence phase. Burn this card if another moon enters play or when this card has no counters. You may shuffle this card from your hand into your library as a discard phase action.

Name: Blood Moon
Cardtype: Event
Moon. Transient.
Put this card in play with 3 counters. Werewolves can burn minions that are not ready as a  action. Burn 1 counter from this card during your influence phase. Burn this card if another moon enters play or when this card has no counters. You may shuffle this card from your hand into your library as a discard phase action.

Name: Gibbous Moon
Cardtype: Event
Moon. Transient.
Werewolves cost 1 less pool to recruit. Burn this card during your influence phase or if another moon enters play. You may shuffle this card from your hand into your library as a discard phase action.

Name: Dark Moon
Cardtype: Event
Moon. Transient.
Put this card in play with 2 counters. Non-unique werewolves can recruit another copy of themselves as if they met the requirement(s). Burn 1 counter from this card during your influence phase. Burn this card if another moon enters play or when this card has no counters. You may shuffle this card from your hand into your library as a discard phase action.

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: Kraus
Messages.Body:
Cool idea!

I like how the wolfies could get some extra punch, and not just in combat; they're still stealable allies and have their obvious problems against proper combat! So something extra is cool.

The problem with the mechanic is that I don't really see any reason for a Moon to be cycled back to your library. Events are one-play-only. So, if you play one of these it's gone for good.

And it's good like that as well; the effects are powerful enough.

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Ankha wrote:
> Name: Gibbous Moon
> Cardtype: Event
> Moon. Transient.
> Werewolves cost 1 less pool to recruit. Burn this card during your influence phase or if another moon enters play. You may shuffle this card from your hand into your library as a discard phase action.
>
This one to me feels quite weak. How many are you expecting to recruit in one turn? 2, 3? To do several in one turn, you'd need to have a whole bunch in hand or close to each other in your library, and that requires quite a high percentage in your deck, or a lot of luck. And you don't generally have that high a percentage, since the non-unique ones are expensive - even with a temporary cost reducer. So is this just 1 or 2 pool - and giving someone else a lucky break with Ossian?

Maybe something like:

Put this card in play with X (5?) counters. Remove a counter each time a werewolf is recruited and the cost is paid to reduce that cost by 1 pool. Remove a counter during your [whatever] phase. Burn this card if it has 0 counters or..

As it stands, it feels like one once per game card that maybe nets you one pool, maybe two. Ascendance-y.

The absolute best case scenario i see is:

Merged petaniqua with concordance and rutors hand( she gets any wolf at minus one, can untap once, and as the crow) has charisma on her. Thats 3 recruit actions for wolves, reduced by 2. So, add another reduction.

You get remnant for 3, renegade for 2, tunnel runner for one(or high top) and other playable wolves are free.

Takes alot of setup. Now, thats barely a "real" deck. In that deck, you save 9 pool. Versus 6 without the moon.

Real wolf decks are garous and tunnel runners. In those, you have maybe 3-4 recruiters and maybe a charisma.

A good turn might see you drop 3 wolves at most, so this is seeing 6 pool in a real best case scenario.

Doesnt hurt things.

But to make wolf decks standalone more, we need an abomination that can recruit any wolf at a reduced cost.

A once-per-game Ascendance which is only useful if you can get a werewolf action through next turn, that is competing against other Events - which are often quite powerful. A strong rushing ally deck is likely to benefit particularly from Dragonbound and several of the other Moon cards. Add Scourge of the Enochians or Uncoiling to taste.
